answers.note: Strong six-stage build-up with draw/say/check at every step, accurate swash-backwash and recurved-end geography, and a blank-diagram retrieval task to finish.
Clear draw-and-say steps, but it leaves out the recurved end, salt marsh and swash/backwash, grows the spit from a 'headland' with a lagoon behind (closer to a bar), and uses sentence-length labels.
Covers every stage accurately with drawing instructions, a script and plenary questions, though the four-panel ASCII layout sits a little awkwardly with the advice to build one growing diagram.
Good short think-aloud and accurate model paragraph, but the 'we do' is mostly an individual writing frame rather than a paragraph the class builds together.
Excellent think-aloud with live self-correction, sequenced shared prompts and a hinge question, but the hinge distractor says rhyme is absent from a line that does rhyme (crawls/walls/falls).
A very full script: detailed think-aloud, step-by-step co-construction using mini-whiteboards, and a separate independent focus on the final line with circulating prompts.

Thorough four-phase plan with accurate definitions, links, spaced retrieval and exam embedding, though it wrongly puts a source in the 4-mark question (sources go in the 5-mark) and gives almost no word origins.
Pairing each Christian term with an Islamic one, plus etymology, non-examples, fix-the-sentence tasks and a six-week retrieval schedule, makes this the most complete plan.
Good word parts and a retrieval schedule, but it defines risalah as 'message' rather than AQA's 'prophethood', some example sentences (e.g. for tawhid) never use the term, and exam guidance is thin.
